title: Tactical Dispositions
coreMove: Make defeat hard before you look for the moment that makes victory easy.
sourcePressure: The source separates protection from attack, teaches that opportunity comes from the opponent, praises winning by making no mistakes, and links measurement through calculation to victory.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating defense as passivity or waiting for luck.

sourceAnchors.name: Measurement to Victory
sourceAnchors.detail: The source lists Measurement, Estimation of quantity, Calculation, Balancing of chances, and Victory as a chain.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Victory starts as measurement long before it looks like force.

sourceAnchors.name: the pound weight and single grain
sourceAnchors.detail: A victorious army against a routed one is compared to a heavy weight against a single grain.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The win should feel heavy before it moves, like the scale already knows which side will drop.

hook: A battlefield metaphor imported into a modern office before the actual choice is visible
A generic sentence about strategy being planning under pressure
counterintuition: The obvious move is not always best; the opposite move is smarter
Winning is not about strength but about strategy
tryThisNow: Set a timer and think about your next battle
Write down your goal and one obstacle
examples: manager staring at a spreadsheet with a coffee cup

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches repeated phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp plus named protagonist plus prop plus decision that makes six examples feel like one example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a direct question, a tactical aside, a second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence

exampleSpecs.domain: architectural firm preparing a public design review
exampleSpecs.audience: project architect defending a controversial housing design
exampleSpecs.stakes: one missing code answer could sink the whole approval
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The scale model sits under fluorescent light while Hannah removes every avoidable defect from the submission before planning her strongest argument.

exampleSpecs.domain: pharmacy chain preventing dispensing errors during a software change
exampleSpecs.stakes: a preventable medication error would outweigh any launch speed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 7:22 a.m., Michael locks the old and new label flows side by side and refuses to launch until the error path is blocked.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two prescription labels with different warning colors

exampleSpecs.domain: documentary producer entering a hostile interview
exampleSpecs.stakes: a factual slip would let the subject dismiss the whole film
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He only needs one crack, Juliette tells the team, then cuts the clever questions until every remaining one is backed by a document.

exampleSpecs.domain: ski patrol deciding whether to open an avalanche-prone bowl
exampleSpecs.stakes: opening too early could put guests below an unstable slope
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Wind-packed snow squeaks under Lukas's skis as he tests the slope until not opening becomes the victory condition.

exampleSpecs.domain: manufacturer qualifying a new supplier before peak season

exampleSpecs.stakes: a cheap part could shut down assembly after contracts are signed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took one brittle gasket from a test batch for Diego to see that the supplier had to lose before the purchase order won.

exampleSpecs.domain: dance company preparing an opening-night lift sequence
exampleSpecs.audience: rehearsal director responsible for dancer safety
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed grip could injure the lead and cancel the run
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Lin lower the music volume, slow the lift, and make the fall path impossible before she lets the dancers chase speed.
